Puerto Nariño · Colombian Amazon

Birdwatching in the Colombian Amazon

An early start, a quieter forest. Listen, look closer and follow the calls.

Ask Amaru on WhatsApp ↗

About this experience

A dedicated birdwatching experience for those who want to spend time listening, watching branches and following the calls of the forest. The focus is on birds, with an early start arranged for your visit. This is a standalone tour, independent of the cacao experience, and sightings vary with the conditions.

The forests and wetlands around Puerto Nariño make an inviting setting for an interest in birds. As one example of the region’s diversity, the Ramsar record for the Tarapoto wetlands documents a rich bird community. That regional picture offers context for your visit; the observation site for Amaru’s birdwatching outing is arranged separately.

Birdwatching begins with a pause. Listen before looking, follow movement among the leaves and allow time for a bird to come into view. The pleasure can be in recognising a call or noticing a detail you would otherwise pass by. Share your interests, whether you are curious to begin or already enjoy keeping your own observation notes.

Destination context sources: Ramsar ↗

What to explore

  • An independent birdwatching experience
  • Early-morning departure arranged together
  • Bring binoculars if you have them; sightings vary

Before you go

Time of day
EARLY MORNING
Duration
Confirm the duration and meeting point with Amaru for your dates.
Physical effort
Moderate effort

Levels are indicative. Terrain, water levels, weather and your group can change the demands of an outing.

Wear discreet colours, suitable walking shoes and rain protection. Bring water and your own binoculars if you have them; ask whether any are available before relying on supplied equipment. Keep voices low and give birds space. Confirm the observation setting, early departure, guide’s experience and walking requirements with Amaru; no particular species is promised.

What should I confirm?

Ask about the route, departure, group requirements, guide language, equipment, transport and what is included. Share your dates and number of travellers, and review the full price and cancellation conditions before confirming anything.

Routes depend on water levels, weather and local conditions. Wildlife sightings cannot be guaranteed.
